[Shared infrastructure]{.eyebrow}

Building shared data and code infrastructure is the first phase of the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd), and the field's most urgent near-term priority. No single existing dataset captures all seven stressor categories across multiple colonies over a full annual cycle. Closing that gap — by integrating what already exists before commissioning anything new — is where the leverage is.

## Datasets in the collaboration

| Dataset | Contributor | Contents | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-hive sensor time series | Julia Fine, USDA ARS | One year, 40 colonies, 15-minute resolution: internal acoustics, temperature, humidity, external apiary conditions; monthly manual population and brood counts | Sharing feasibility under evaluation |
| Multi-year colony measurements | Gloria DeGrandi-Hoffman, USDA ARS / ASU | Frame counts, *Varroa* levels, pollen data, virus data, organised against corresponding publications | Being organised for release |
| Dataset crosswalk / inventory | Kang, DeGrandi-Hoffman, Flenniken | Variables measured, temporal resolution, colony counts, geographic coverage, formats across all participating labs | In progress — Phase I deliverable |

## Software targets

| Tool | Lead | Description | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline colony model | Kang, Parshad, Pal | Reference implementation of the healthy-colony ODE framework with modular stressor extensions | 6 months |
| Early warning pipeline | Group 4 | Time series and machine learning pipeline for detecting pre-collapse signatures in sensor streams | 12 months |
| Beescape deep learning extension | Li, Group 5 | Deep learning on aerial imagery for flowering species richness prediction | 12 months |
| Beekeeper decision tool | Groups 2 & 4 + industry | Operational decision rules for treatment timing and split decisions | 18–24 months |

Code released by the collaboration will be published in this GitHub organisation with open licences and reproducible environments.

## Pollinator research and landscape tools

- [**Penn State Center for Pollinator Research**](https://pollinators.psu.edu/) — research, extension, diagnostic, classroom, image, and decision-support resources for pollinator health.
- [**Beescape**](https://pollinators.psu.edu/resources-tools/beescape) — Penn State's GIS decision-support tool for exploring seasonal forage, nesting resources, insecticide load, weather, and pollination value around a location.
- [**BeeSpatial**](https://pollinators.psu.edu/research/beeshiny) — researcher-focused access to county-level climate, land-use, and habitat-quality indicators across the continental United States.

## Models, software, and federal data

- [**BEEPOP+**](https://beepop.ars.usda.gov/) — USDA ARS web model for simulating honey bee colony demography, weather, *Varroa*, management, and pesticide scenarios.
- [**BEEHAVE**](https://beehave-model.net/) — open NetLogo systems model linking within-hive colony dynamics with foraging in dynamic landscapes and multiple stressors.
- [**USDA National Agricultural Library: Apiculture and Beekeeping**](https://www.nal.usda.gov/animal-health-and-welfare/beekeeping) — gateway to USDA bee reports, surveys, Ag Data Commons records, federal research programs, and modeling tools.
- [**USGS Bee Lab**](https://www.usgs.gov/labs/usgs-bee-lab-at-the-eastern-ecological-science-center) — native-bee inventory, monitoring, identification, survey design, occurrence records, images, and bee–plant association resources.

## Monitoring and community science

- [**Bumble Bee Watch**](https://www.bumblebeewatch.org/) — submit and explore expert-reviewed bumble bee observations to support North American distribution and conservation research.
- [**USGS Bee Inventories and Monitoring Projects**](https://www.usgs.gov/labs/native-bee-inventory-and-monitoring-lab/bee-inventories-and-monitoring-projects) — examples, protocols, and partnerships for bee inventory and monitoring projects.

## Conservation, risk, and education

- [**EPA Pollinator Protection**](https://www.epa.gov/pollinator-protection) — pesticide risk assessment, mitigation, managed pollinator protection plans, best practices, and bee-kill reporting resources.
- [**Xerces Pollinator Conservation Resource Center**](https://www.xerces.org/pollinator-resource-center) — region-specific plant lists, habitat-establishment guidance, publications, and seed-source information.
- [**Pollinator Partnership Resources**](https://www.pollinator.org/resources) — ecoregional planting guides, bee identification materials, education resources, habitat tools, and grant information.
- [**American Institute of Mathematics**](https://aimath.org/) — host of the 2026 workshop that launched this collaboration.

::: {.panel}
[Contributing data]{.eyebrow}

If you hold colony monitoring data — sensor streams, inspection records, treatment logs, loss records — and would consider contributing it to the crosswalk, please [contact us](contact.qmd). Contribution to the inventory does not require making data public; the first step is simply documenting what exists.
:::
